hypotheses.paper: M_0 globally hyperbolic singular flat spacetime
hypotheses.note: as in CBG/Geometry's cbg: abstract Geometry (DEC-60), a Cauchy surface S, M_0 T2, connected, second countable; cbg_proof has cbg's statement verbatim

hypotheses.paper: Sbierski Lemma 3.3 (the MCGHD morphisms psi_ik are injective) is PROVED there from the Lorentzian structure (a time function on each GHD); l.1157 then uses the embedding property
hypotheses.note: Lemma 3.3 is proved from the interface field Geometry.timeFunction (interface round 2 (1): every T2, connected, second-countable, globally hyperbolic admissible spacetime has a continuous time function strictly increasing along ≤): mcghdInjective (mcghdMap_injOn, IsCGHD.injOn). cbg carries no hypothesis. The construction keeps MCGHDInjective as a proof parameter (always mcghdInjective)

hypotheses.paper: inductive limit of the directed family (ETT.tex:2336-2340)
hypotheses.note: realised as Sbierski's gluing of all SmallDev along pairwise MCGHDs; the universal property is DEC-59's IsUniversal, with unique morphisms
Dev.IsUniversal.existsUnique_iso: the isomorphism is moreover unique; ETT form cbg_proof_ett
Geometry.secondCountable_of_cauchy (gx C2), applied after GH and the Cauchy surface are proved

findings: Sbierski's transitivity of (3.15) (pdftotext l.1166-1170) asserts that U_ik ∩ psi_ik^{-1}(U_kl) with psi_kl∘psi_ik is a CGHD; that needs iota(Sigma) to be a Cauchy surface of an intersection of two Cauchy inclusions, the existence half CBG/CausalConvex leaves open. Proved instead (mcghd_cocycle): agreement on U_ij ∩ U_ik via the ppcm of N_j, N_k (rigidity), and U_ij ∩ psi^{-1}(U_jk) ⊆ U_ik by an open-closed argument on this connected set (lem:C_ext_connexe) whose closed half is the Hausdorffness of the ppcm of N_i, N_k (Thm 3.13).

ETT's proof of theo:CBG (ETT.tex:2336-2340) asserts the inductive limit is maximal and M_0 -> limit is a Cauchy embedding without argument; global hyperbolicity of the limit (with i(Sigma) Cauchy) is a genuine step: proved here (maxStr_globallyHyperbolic, maxStr_isCauchySurface) by a family exit/re-entry argument on chains (Causality.ManyPiece), BEFORE second countability and without curvesExtend / isCompact_* on the limit (the design section 6 package-10 risk, resolved).

Sbierski step 4 reduces a cover of a curve segment to two pieces using timelike curves; in ETT's GH (causal + compact diamonds) the needed fact is that every diamond J(p,q), p ∈ O_i, q ∈ O_j, lies in O_i ∪ O_j (ManyPiece.mem_or_mem), which follows from the side of a point w.r.t. Sigma being piece-independent.

kb_proposals: An intersection of two Cauchy inclusions is not known to be one (CausalConvex's open existence half); avoid it: get cocycle-type inclusions from connectedness (lem:C_ext_connexe) plus Hausdorffness of the relevant pair gluing (limits of ι₁ a = ι₂ (g a) agree in a T2 gluing).

Global hyperbolicity of a gluing of a family without curve extension on the glued space: Causality.ManyPiece (CBG/Maximal) — the side of a point w.r.t. the common Cauchy set is piece-independent, so chains can be pushed into one piece from either end; diamonds then live in two pieces and package 7's mixed decomposition applies.
